title: Acquire complete microbial sepiolite and phlogopite dissolution evidence
body:
Two microbial clay-weathering studies remain deferred because their complete original figures or full text could not be inspected. The new sepiolite record accepts only the complete primary abiotic study by Mulders and Oelkers (2020), DOI 10.1016/j.gca.2019.11.026. This is an evidence-acquisition follow-up, not a defect in that accepted scope.

- **Sepiolite:** Nejadasadi et al. (2021), *Sepiolite Dissolution by Different Silicate Solubilizing Bacteria*, DOI [10.1007/s42729-021-00602-0](https://doi.org/10.1007/s42729-021-00602-0). Publisher routes returned subscription HTML. The author-uploaded ResearchGate PDF was readable through a text parser as 15 pages, but local retrieval returned 403 and no inspectable graphics were obtained. Check original diffraction, figures, tables and supplements; mineral impurities; uninoculated and mineral-free controls; medium and pH effects; organism and strain identities; and the reported unchanged bulk structure over 15 days.
- **Phlogopite:** Balland-Bolou-Bi et al. (2019), *Increased Mg release rates and related Mg isotopic signatures during bacteria-phlogopite interactions*, DOI [10.1016/j.chemgeo.2018.12.020](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chemgeo.2018.12.020). HAL metadata confirms [hal-01968263v1](https://hal.science/hal-01968263v1) and a deposited PDF, but the document routes returned challenge HTML; the publisher accepted-manuscript route returned 403. Acquire the complete methods, figures, tables and supplements to assess mineral composition, four strain identities, viable biomass, organic-acid and pH controls, and release/isotope denominators. Existing biotite-group evidence cannot substitute for this mineral-species experiment.

Acceptance: obtain legitimate inspectable originals, retain their hashes and version/rights metadata, independently check all claim-bearing graphics and supplemental data, verify identifiers and correction/conflict searches, then curate only supported claims with canonical history and an independent scientific review. Keep partial text access distinct from complete graphics review. A microbial sepiolite update and a phlogopite record are conditional outcomes, not quotas.

Evidence dossier: `research/sources/round78-silicates/20261014T180444Z.{json,md}` in the pending round78 publication. A fresh all-state paginated GitHub issue scan and hidden/ignored local search found no existing matching issue within those scopes. Raw articles remain outside Git.

title: Correct the 2019 electron-donor survey duration in chukanovite
body:
The chukanovite record describes the 2019 lepidocrocite experiment as a “72-day electron-donor survey”. In O’Loughlin et al. (2019), DOI 10.3390/min9070434, Section 3.1 (PDF page 4) uses 72 days specifically for the no-exogenous-electron-donor result. Figure 1 (page 5) plots N-acetylglucosamine and sterile-control observations extending to approximately 98 days. The whole survey therefore does not have one common 72-day endpoint.

Acceptance: replace the survey-wide duration with wording that preserves differing observation periods; retain the separate focused 62-day formate experiments and bounded chukanovite nondetection. Append canonical EDIT and inline history, preserve CREATE and the initial native finding, pass affected checks, and save an independent successor linked to the exact F1 occurrence. This is a minor contextual error and does not invalidate the separate 2021 goethite product assignment.


Independent initial observation: `reviews/structured/20261014T181104Z-chukanovite-round78-initial/review.yaml`, finding F1, stable key `chukanovite-round78-donor-survey-duration`. The record and companion source dossier wording will be corrected; the initial observation remains immutable.

title: Correct canonical target IDs in round78 clay review successors
body:
Two saved round78 scientific reviews use bare slugs (`palygorskite` and `saponite`) as target IDs. The native saver accepts generic IDs, but exact corpus coverage requires the maintained owner IDs `cmmmech:palygorskite` and `cmmmech:saponite`. Their source evidence and owner/history hashes remain correct.

Affected immutable bundles:

- `reviews/structured/20261014T181353Z-palygorskite-round78-independent/`
- `reviews/structured/20261014T181355Z-saponite-round78-independent/`

The initial metadata finding RM1, exact hashes and acceptance criteria are retained in `reviews/publication/20261014-round78/20261014T181524Z-clay-review-id-initial.{json,md}`.

Acceptance: preserve both original observations and RM1; append scientific review successors with canonical IDs throughout targets, reviewed scope, checks and assessments; explicitly link the earlier reviews; independently verify that only metadata and current check/provenance statements change; pass the full native review checker and exact-ID/path/hash coverage. No maintained owner edits or invented scientific findings are required.
